hostLink.fixIntro: Run these on {{host}} itself, not in this terminal, or hand the prompt to Claude Code or Codex on that machine.
hostLink.install: If it is stopped, reinstall and start it:
hostLink.prompt:
The Oppenheimer runner on {{host}} has lost its link to Oppenheimer. Help me get it back.

- First tell me which machine you are on (uname -n, whoami). If it is not {{host}}, stop.
- Run ~/.local/bin/oppenheimer-runner status and show me what it prints.
- Read the last 50 lines of ~/.oppenheimer/log/runner.log and ~/.oppenheimer/log/runner.err.log
  and tell me what went wrong.
- Do not reinstall, uninstall or run anything as root unless I say so. If the service is
  stopped, propose ~/.local/bin/oppenheimer-runner install and wait for my go-ahead.

data.account: Account and identity data, such as your name, work email, profile picture, authentication provider and organization membership.
data.content: Content entered or uploaded by your organization, including notes, messages and attachments where those features are used.
data.integrations: Connection details and tokens for third-party services that an authorized user chooses to connect.
data.intro: The data we process depends on how you and your organization use the service. It may include:
data.technical: Technical and security data, including IP address, browser information, timestamps, session records, error logs and security events.
data.title: 2. Data we process
data.workspace: Workspace data, including team roles, permissions, settings, audit events and activity needed to provide the service.

google.body: If you choose Google Sign-In, Google provides your name, email address, profile picture and provider identifiers. We use this information only to authenticate you, protect access and create or match your profile. We do not sell this data or use it for advertising.
google.separateConsent: Google Sign-In does not grant access to Gmail, Drive or any other Google service. If your organization later enables a supported Google integration, we request the relevant permissions through a separate consent screen and use that data only to provide the integration you selected.
google.title: 3. Google Sign-In and Google user data

purposes.body: We process data to provide and administer the service, authenticate users, support team collaboration, keep the service secure, respond to requests and comply with law. Depending on the context, our legal basis is performance of a contract, our legitimate interests in operating and securing the service, consent where required, or compliance with a legal obligation.
purposes.title: 4. Purposes and legal bases

retention.body: We keep account and workspace data while the relevant account or organization is active and for the limited period needed for security, recovery, dispute resolution and legal obligations. Deleted data may remain in encrypted backups until those backups expire through their normal cycle. Integration credentials are removed when the connection is deleted, subject to short-lived operational backups.
retention.title: 6. How long we keep data

rights.authority: You may also lodge a complaint with the Spanish Data Protection Agency (AEPD) or your local supervisory authority.
rights.body: Where applicable, you may request access, correction, deletion, restriction or portability of your personal data, object to certain processing, or withdraw consent without affecting earlier lawful processing. Contact us from the email associated with your account so we can verify and answer your request.
rights.title: 9. Your privacy rights

security.body: We use technical and organizational safeguards designed to protect data, including encrypted connections, access controls, isolated infrastructure, secret management, security logging and restricted administrative access. No system can guarantee absolute security, but we review and improve these measures as the service evolves.
security.title: 8. Security

sharing.body: We share data only when needed to operate the service, comply with law or follow your organization's instructions. Providers may include the hosting, storage, authentication, email and integration providers your organization enables. Some providers may process data outside the European Economic Area using applicable safeguards such as adequacy decisions or standard contractual clauses. We do not sell personal data.
sharing.title: 5. Service providers and international transfers
